rationale: A wins because it finds the sharper regulatory split and does not pretend the launch is bigger than the facts: "Whoop puts a cleared ECG and an uncleared blood-pressure estimate on the same wrist" is the real story hiding in plain sight. B has good bones, especially "Whoop's new blood-pressure number isn't a medical reading — and needs a cuff to even start," but it decorates with unsupported furniture like "Apple Watch / Samsung / Fitbit" and "screenless band." A is not perfect; "What Whoop's cardiologists actually signed off on" overstates a review as sign-off. But A gives a founder four usable press shapes with hard proof gates, while B gives three and needs more cleanup before anyone should send it near a reporter.
gaps_in_A: "What Whoop's cardiologists actually signed off on" inflates "reviewed the features" into sign-off. A review is not approval, endorsement, or clinical blessing.
"what a privately held company last valued at $3.6B needs from parity to hold a subscription base" leans into business speculation without subscriber, retention, or competitive-pressure facts.

"the downstream load it puts on clinics: false positives, worried-well referrals" is a legitimate clinical line of inquiry, but those effects are not in the supplied update and need to be framed more explicitly as questions, not givens.
gaps_in_B: "Apple Watch / Samsung / Fitbit" names competitors the update did not supply. Maybe true in the real world, but in this exercise that is an invented specificity penalty.
"form factor, screenless band, subscription model" imports product-positioning facts not in the update. The membership tier is supplied; screenless-band differentiation is not.
"the wearable was supposed to replace" turns a consumer assumption into a fact. The update says cuff calibration is required; it does not say Whoop claimed replacement.
"health features are increasingly paywalled" is a trend claim built from one Whoop fact. B admits it needs more than one company, but the headline angle still reaches beyond the record.
